comparisons.peer_summary: AMD continued investing in the open ROCm software stack, making key optimizations and adding features in the latest release to improve performance for generative AI workloads and simplify the developer experience.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD describe their strategic shift toward comprehensive, full-stack software ecosystems to accelerate AI workloads. NVIDIA defines its full stack as including the foundational CUDA programming model, GPU hardware, and domain-specific libraries to accelerate AI training and inference. Similarly, AMD describes its investment in the open ROCm software stack as a key component to deliver powerful AI training and inference capabilities on its platforms. While NVIDIA emphasizes its proprietary CUDA ecosystem, AMD highlights its open-source ROCm stack, but both identify the integration of software with their respective hardware architectures as critical for addressing generative AI and computational workloads.

sentences.text: Our full-stack includes the foundational CUDA programming model that runs on all NVIDIA GPUs, as well as hundreds of domain-specific software libraries, software development kits, or SDKs, and Application Programming Interfaces, or APIs.

This deep and broad software stack accelerates the performance and eases the deployment of NVIDIA accelerated computing for computationally intensive workloads such as artificial intelligence, or AI, model training and inference, data analytics, scientific computing, and 3D graphics, with vertical-specific optimizations to address industries ranging from healthcare and telecom to automotive and manufacturing.

We continued to invest in driving software capabilities and the open ecosystem to deliver powerful new features and capabilities in the AMD ROCm™ open software stack, bringing the latest features to highly-performant AI training and inference on AMD platforms.

During the year, we made several key optimizations and additional features in the latest AMD ROCm software that increases performance in key generative AI workloads, adds expanded support and optimization for additional frameworks and libraries, and simplifies the overall developer experience.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Tanzu Platform accelerates software delivery with enhanced governance and operational efficiency, includes Tanzu AI Solutions for generative AI applications, and offers full-stack visibility and lifecycle management across clouds.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies utilize the term 'full-stack' to describe their complete technology offerings, though their specific components differ based on their business focus. NVIDIA describes itself as a 'full-stack computing infrastructure company' whose stack includes the CUDA programming model, GPUs, and software libraries for data-center-scale AI. Broadcom describes its Tanzu Platform as offering 'full-stack visibility' from applications to infrastructure, including Tanzu AI Solutions for generative AI. Both disclosures emphasize the importance of a complete, integrated software and infrastructure layer to support AI and data-centric workloads.

sentences.text: NVIDIA is now a full-stack computing infrastructure company with data-center-scale offerings that are reshaping industry.

Our full-stack includes the foundational CUDA programming model that runs on all NVIDIA GPUs, as well as hundreds of domain-specific software libraries, software development kits, or SDKs, and Application Programming Interfaces, or APIs.

• Tanzu Platform: This cloud native application platform accelerates software delivery, providing platform engineering teams with enhanced governance and operational efficiency while reducing toil and complexity for development teams. Tanzu Platform includes access to content including enterprise-ready curated distributions of open source software technologies used for storing and processing data. It also includes Tanzu AI Solutions, a set of capabilities that help application teams deliver generative AI-powered, intelligent applications quickly, safely, and at scale. Tanzu Platform also offers teams full-stack visibility from applications to infrastructure and efficient modern application lifecycle management across public and private clouds with Cloud Foundry and/or with any conformant Kubernetes.

comparisons.peer_topic: Software strategy and open source contributions
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel aims to optimize AI frameworks and maintains the OpenVINO toolkit for deep learning inference. In 2024, Intel launched the Open Platform for Enterprise AI under the Linux Foundation and contributed oneAPI specifications to the UXL Foundation to enable open, multi-vendor programming across accelerators.
comparisons.comparison: NVIDIA and Intel both explicitly discuss their comprehensive software stacks designed to optimize hardware performance for AI and multi-vendor ecosystems. NVIDIA highlights its 'deep and broad software stack' including CUDA to accelerate AI workloads. Intel describes its 'oneAPI' as an open programming model that serves as a software stack to enable developers to create performant cross-architecture applications across CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators. Both companies frame their software stacks as critical enablers for their hardware platforms, though NVIDIA focuses on its proprietary CUDA ecosystem for AI acceleration while Intel emphasizes its open, multi-vendor oneAPI standard.

sentences.text: Our full-stack includes the foundational CUDA programming model that runs on all NVIDIA GPUs, as well as hundreds of domain-specific software libraries, software development kits, or SDKs, and Application Programming Interfaces, or APIs.

This deep and broad software stack accelerates the performance and eases the deployment of NVIDIA accelerated computing for computationally intensive workloads such as artificial intelligence, or AI, model training and inference, data analytics, scientific computing, and 3D graphics, with vertical-specific optimizations to address industries ranging from healthcare and telecom to automotive and manufacturing.

Most of these frameworks and middleware are built from our oneAPI, which enables developers to create performant cross-architecture applications using a single code base across CPUs, GPUs, and other accelerators.
By doing so, oneAPI delivers an open and multi-vendor programming model enabling choice and code re-use across the accelerator hardware ecosystem.
